intro: The Ghana Education Service (GES) Kindergarten curriculum is designed for children aged 4–6 years. It focuses on play-based learning across six key areas, helping children develop physically, socially, emotionally, and intellectually.

classes.name: KG 1
classes.focus: Introduction to structured learning through play and exploration.

classes.name: KG 2
classes.focus: Building on KG 1 foundations, preparing for Primary 1.

learningAreas.name: Language and Literacy
learningAreas.description: Listening, speaking, early reading and writing.
kg1: Listening to and following simple instructions
kg2: Recognising all letters and their sounds
Blending sounds to read simple words
Writing simple words and short sentences
Retelling a story in own words

learningAreas.name: Numeracy
kg1: Sorting objects by size, colour, shape

learningAreas.name: Creative Arts
learningAreas.description: Drawing, music, dance, drama, and imaginative play.
kg2: Making simple crafts with paper and glue

learningAreas.name: Our World Our People
learningAreas.description: Understanding self, family, community, and environment.
kg1: Learning about the home and school
kg2: Understanding roles in family and community
Naming common foods and their sources
Care for the environment (plants, animals, water)
Recognising safety rules at home and school

learningAreas.name: Physical Development
learningAreas.description: Gross motor skills, fine motor skills, and healthy habits.
kg2: Understanding personal hygiene (washing hands, brushing teeth)

themes.name: All About Me
themes.description: My body, my senses, my feelings, my name.

themes.name: My Family and Community
themes.description: Family members, neighbours, helpers in the community.

themes.name: Our World and Environment
themes.description: Plants, animals, weather, water, and caring for our world.

themes.name: Festivals and Celebrations
themes.description: Ghanaian festivals, national days, and cultural celebrations.

themes.name: Health and Safety
themes.description: Personal hygiene, healthy habits, and safety rules.

themes.name: Food and Nutrition
themes.description: Common foods, where they come from, and healthy eating.

themes.name: Transport and Communication
themes.description: Ways we travel, ways we communicate.

teachingApproach: Learning through play — songs, games, stories
Hands-on activities, not just sitting and listening
Small group work and one-on-one attention
Use of local language and materials
assessmentNote: KG assessment is observation-based. Teachers watch how children play, talk, and interact — not formal tests. The goal is growth, confidence, and a love of learning.
